<Gauge> shows a value as a bar along an arc or a ring, between a minimum and a maximum, with threshold markers, labels and a sparkline. It is a port of Grafana 12's Gauge panel; see Coming from Grafana.

use bui_charts::*;

class, key

Shape and bar

  • GaugeShape::Gauge draws a 220° arc open at the bottom; Circle a full ring starting at the top. Both start from min and run clockwise.
  • The bar fills the arc from min to the value; the rest is a grey track. With neutral, the bar runs from the neutral value to the value in either direction, for balances, deltas and temperatures around zero.
  • bar_width_factor sets the thickness: the bar is bar_width_factor × radius ÷ 3 wide.
  • BarShape::Rounded gives the bar round ends. The Point endpoint marker, a small dot at each end, only shows on rounded bars.
  • segment_count above 1 splits the arc into separate segments. Each lit segment takes the colour its own value would have, so thresholds show as bands. Segments are never drawn thinner than 3 px; the count is reduced to fit.

Thresholds and colour

  • The bar's colour comes from a matching mapping, otherwise from color, as in Bar Gauge.
  • show_threshold_markers draws a thin ring outside the bar in each threshold step's colour, so you can see how close the value is to the next step. It is hidden when min equals max.
  • show_threshold_labels writes min, each threshold and max around the arc, formatted with format / decimals. Percentage thresholds are written as percentages. With neutral, its value is labelled too.

Effects

GaugeEffects switches on Grafana's three visual effects:

effects={GaugeEffects::new().gradient().bar_glow()}
effects={GaugeEffects::all()}
EffectLook
gradientthe bar is shaded along the arc: through the threshold colours, along the scheme, or from a darker to a lighter tone of the value's colour
bar_glowa soft halo around the bar
center_glowa faint radial glow of the value's colour inside the gauge

EndpointMarker::Glow adds a bright spot at the end of the bar, in dark themes.

Text and sparkline

  • The value is centred in the gauge and sized to fit. text_mode Auto adds the name when there are several gauges or a name accessor; Name, Value, ValueAndName and None choose directly. value_size and title_size fix the sizes.
  • With sparkline and several rows, a small chart of the history sits under the value, in the value's colour.

Several gauges

Every value gets its own gauge. BarOrientation::Auto packs them into the grid that keeps them closest to square; Horizontal stacks them as rows; Vertical places them side by side. Sizing::Manual { min_width, min_height, .. } stops them from shrinking below that size. With several gauges, all values use the size of the longest text, so they line up.

examples.title: Gauge
examples.description: The last CPU reading on a 220° arc with threshold markers and a sparkline.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn basic() {
    let data = use_signal(samples(1));
    rsx! {
        <Gauge data={data} value={|s: &Sample| s.cpu} x={|s: &Sample| s.time} thresholds={Thresholds::absolute(&LOAD[..])} format={percent} class="h-56" />
    }
}

examples.title: Effects
examples.description: Gradient, bar glow, centre glow and a glowing endpoint.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn effects() {
    let data = use_signal(samples(5));
    rsx! {
        <Gauge
            data={data}
            value={|s: &Sample| s.temperature}
            x={|s: &Sample| s.time}
            min={0.}
            max={100.}
            effects={GaugeEffects::all()}
            bar_shape={BarShape::Rounded}
            endpoint_marker={EndpointMarker::Glow}
            thresholds={Thresholds::absolute(&HEAT[..])}
            format={celsius}
            class="h-56"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Neutral point
examples.description: The bar grows from 0 in either direction.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn neutral() {
    let data = use_signal(samples(7));
    rsx! {
        <Gauge
            data={data}
            value={|s: &Sample| s.balance}
            x={|s: &Sample| s.time}
            min={-50.}
            max={50.}
            neutral={0.}
            show_threshold_markers={false}
            show_threshold_labels={true}
            color={GaugeColor::Scheme(Scheme::RedYellowGreen)}
            decimals={1}
            class="h-56"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: A signal as data: the gauge redraws when it changes.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live() {
    let round = use_signal(1u64);
    let data = use_signal(samples(1));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-64">
            <div
                id="next"
                class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline"
                onClick={move || {
                    let next = round.get() + 1;
                    round.set(next);
                    data.set(samples(next));
                }}
            >
                "Load new readings"
            </div>
            <Gauge data={data} value={|s: &Sample| s.cpu} x={|s: &Sample| s.time} bar_shape={BarShape::Rounded} effects={GaugeEffects::new().gradient()} thresholds={Thresholds::absolute(&LOAD[..])} format={percent} class="flex-1" />
        </div>
    }
}
